newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia raises export concerns with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia raises export concerns with Clinton.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday he had raised concerns over U.S. agricultural export subsidy programmes in talks with President Bill Clinton.
Howard told Clinton such programmes harmed Australians exports and the farm sector, the Australian leader told reporters at a joint news conference.
"It is the fact that the Australian government believes the existing arrangements do work against the interests of major primary producers such as Australia," Howard said.
"I think it is fair to add that the prime source of the problem is not to be found in the United States but rather within the European Union," he said.
Clinton said he had made a commitment that free trade nations would not be hurt by use of the subsidies, such as the U.S. Export Enhancement Program (EEP).
Washington has previously said the subsidies are aimed at countering subsidies by the European Union and would not be used to break into traditional Australian markets.

"I committed to the prime minister and ... the people of Australia that we are going to do everything we can to make sure that any future use of these programmes is not, either directly or indirectly, working to the disadvantage of a country that is innocent of any wrong-doing, in this case Australia," Clinton said.

"I look forward to the day when we will have a genuinely open market in agriculture which would help your agricultural interests and the American agricultural interests and I believe would work to the benefit of the entire world," he said.
